group.title: History and tradition
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A family member who lived long ago, before your grandparents.
examples: My {ancestors} came from a small village in the north.
wrong: My ancestor is my baby nephew who was born last week.

words.meaning: The family members and origins you come from.
examples: She is proud of her Irish {ancestry}.
wrong: His ancestry is the list of his future grandchildren.

words.meaning: A line of rulers from the same family.
examples: The {dynasty} ruled the country for three hundred years.
wrong: The dynasty lasted only one morning and had one king.

words.meaning: A group of countries ruled by one powerful leader or state.
examples: The Roman {Empire} stretched across Europe.
wrong: The empire was one small village with no ruler.

words.meaning: A long period of history with a special character.
examples: The invention of the car began a new {era} in travel.
wrong: The era lasted just five minutes.

words.meaning: From the Middle Ages, about the years 500 to 1500.
examples: We visited a {medieval} castle with thick stone walls.
wrong: The medieval building was built in 2020.

words.meaning: An object made by people long ago, kept for its history.
examples: The museum shows {artifacts} from ancient Egypt.
wrong: The artifact was a modern phone bought yesterday.

words.meaning: The study of the past by digging up old objects and buildings.
examples: She studied {archaeology} and now works on old sites.
wrong: Archaeology is the study of future cities in space.

words.meaning: A society with its own culture, laws and way of life.
examples: The Maya built a great {civilization} in Central America.
wrong: The civilization had no culture, rules or people.

words.meaning: A country or area ruled by another, more powerful country.
examples: The island was once a British {colony}.
wrong: The colony was a free country that no other nation ever ruled.

words.meaning: A system where a king or queen is head of state.
examples: The country has been a {monarchy} for centuries.
wrong: In this monarchy, there has never been a king or queen.

words.meaning: The period when a king or queen rules.
examples: Many castles were built during her {reign}.
wrong: The queen’s reign ended many years before she was crowned.

words.meaning: A sudden change of government, often by force.
examples: The {revolution} ended the king’s rule.
wrong: The revolution kept everything exactly as it was.

words.meaning: To take control of a country or people by force.
examples: The army {conquered} the city after a long siege.
wrong: They conquered the land by losing every battle.

words.meaning: An attack in which an army enters another country.
examples: The {invasion} began at dawn.
wrong: The invasion was a friendly visit by tourists.

words.meaning: To dig in the ground to find old objects or buildings.
examples: Experts {excavated} a Roman villa under the field.
wrong: They excavated the site by building a car park on top.

words.meaning: A time in the past when something was at its best.
examples: The 1950s were the {golden age} of cinema.
wrong: The golden age was the worst time in the country’s history.

words.meaning: A written record of events in the order they happened.
examples: A monk wrote a {chronicle} of the town’s history.
wrong: The chronicle was a list of events in random order.

words.meaning: A person related to someone who lived long ago.
examples: He is a {descendant} of a famous sailor.
wrong: She is a descendant of her own granddaughter.

words.meaning: The old stories, beliefs and customs of a people.
examples: Dragons appear often in local {folklore}.
wrong: Folklore is a new law passed by parliament last year.

words.meaning: A set of actions always done in the same way, often for a ceremony.
examples: Lighting candles is part of the wedding {ritual}.
wrong: The ritual changes completely every time it’s done.

words.meaning: A valuable object passed down in a family for many years.
examples: This ring is a family {heirloom} from my grandmother.
wrong: The heirloom is a cheap toy I bought this morning.

words.meaning: One of the first people to do something or go somewhere.
examples: She was a {pioneer} of women’s aviation.
wrong: He was a pioneer, so he did it long after everyone else.

words.meaning: From the time before people wrote history down.
examples: We saw {prehistoric} cave paintings.
wrong: The prehistoric tools were made last year.

words.meaning: To officially end a law, system or custom.
examples: The country {abolished} the death penalty decades ago.
wrong: They abolished the tax by raising it.

words.meaning: Freedom of a country from rule by another country.
examples: The nation celebrates its {independence} every summer.
wrong: After independence, the country was ruled by its old masters.

words.meaning: A written agreement between countries.
examples: The two nations signed a peace {treaty}.
wrong: The treaty was a war that broke out between them.

words.meaning: A collection of old records and documents, or the place they are kept.
examples: The town {archive} holds letters from the 1800s.
wrong: The archive is a bin where old papers are destroyed.

words.meaning: A person who studies and writes about the past.
examples: The {historian} wrote a book about the war.
wrong: The historian studies only what will happen next year.

words.meaning: To do something to remember and honor a past event or person.
examples: A statue {commemorates} the soldiers who died.
wrong: They commemorated the hero by forgetting his name.

words.meaning: The date when something happened in an earlier year.
examples: The city celebrates its 500th {anniversary} this year.
wrong: The anniversary is the first day the event ever happened.

words.meaning: A man who rules an empire.
examples: The {emperor} ruled over many lands and peoples.
wrong: The emperor was a farmer with no power over anyone.

words.meaning: To keep something in its original state.
examples: The village has {preserved} its old traditions.
wrong: They preserved the old church by knocking it down.

words.meaning: The work of repairing an old building or object.
examples: The {restoration} of the palace took ten years.
wrong: The restoration left the painting more damaged than before.

words.meaning: An old story about famous people or events that may not be true.
examples: According to {legend}, a giant built the bridge.
wrong: The legend is a news report about what happened today.

words.meaning: A group of families with the same language and customs.
examples: The {tribe} has lived in the valley for centuries.
wrong: The tribe was one person who lived alone.

words.meaning: In the past, a poor farmer who worked on the land.
examples: Most {peasants} worked on land owned by a lord.
wrong: The peasant was the richest lord in the kingdom.

words.meaning: In the Middle Ages, a soldier of high rank who fought on a horse.
examples: The {knight} rode into battle in shining armor.
wrong: The knight had never ridden a horse or held a sword.

words.meaning: Important in history, or famous because of the past.
examples: The moon landing was a {historic} moment.
wrong: It was a historic day that nobody will remember.

words.meaning: To give knowledge or objects to younger people in a family.
examples: The recipe was {passed down} from my great-grandmother.
wrong: The stories were passed down from children to their great-grandparents.
